name: part_standards
question:
The part to check, "1.3 Exclusions from Confidential Information":
<part>
<paragraph id="b5" number="§1.3">
<now>Information shall not be Confidential Information if it: (a) is or becomes public other than as a result of a breach of this Agreement; (b) was already lawfully held by the Recipient prior to disclosure; (c) is lawfully obtained from a third party who is free to disclose it; or (d) is developed independently by the Recipient without reference to the Discloser's Confidential Information.</now>
</paragraph>
</part>

Our approved clauses closest to it:
<approved_clause id="nda-exclusions" title="Exclusions from Confidential Information">
Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Agreement; (b) was lawfully in the Recipient's possession before disclosure; (c) is lawfully received from a third party without restriction; or (d) is independently developed by the Recipient without use of the Discloser's Confidential Information.
</approved_clause>

Our standard positions:
<standard_position id="pb-governing-law" title="Governing law and jurisdiction">
Our standard: Law of England and Wales, with the courts of England and Wales having exclusive jurisdiction.
Acceptable fallback: Law of Ireland or Scotland; or English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction. Any US state law needs General Counsel sign-off.
Red flags: Any US state law; Exclusive jurisdiction of courts outside the UK; Arbitration seated outside London
</standard_position>
<standard_position id="pb-confidentiality-term" title="Duration of confidentiality obligations">
Our standard: Obligations survive for 3 years after termination or expiry; trade secrets protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.
Acceptable fallback: Anywhere from 2 to 5 years after termination.
Red flags: Perpetual obligations for all information; Less than 2 years; No survival clause
</standard_position>
<standard_position id="pb-mutuality" title="Mutuality">
Our standard: Every confidentiality obligation, restriction and remedy applies equally to both parties.
Acceptable fallback: None. A one-way NDA must be on our one-way template.
Red flags: Obligations that bind only PortSwigger; Remedies or indemnities available to one party only
</standard_position>
<standard_position id="pb-residuals" title="Residuals">
Our standard: No residuals clause. The Recipient may not use Confidential Information retained in memory outside the Purpose.
Acceptable fallback: None. We have never accepted a residuals clause; escalate to General Counsel.
Red flags: Right to use information retained in unaided memory; Any "notwithstanding" language that frees use of Confidential Information
</standard_position>
<standard_position id="pb-non-solicit" title="Non-solicitation of staff">
Our standard: No non-solicitation clause.
Acceptable fallback: Mutual, no more than 12 months, limited to staff directly involved, with a carve-out for general job advertisements.
Red flags: One-way restriction on PortSwigger; Longer than 12 months; Liquidated damages or hiring fees; No carve-out for general advertising
</standard_position>

<part>
<paragraph id="b12" number="Section 2.05">
<now>Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict either Party from using, for any purpose, any information retained in the unaided memory of its Representatives who had access to Confidential Information, including ideas, concepts, know-how and techniques contained therein.</now>
</paragraph>
</part>

Our approved clauses closest to it:
<approved_clause id="nda-obligations" title="Confidentiality obligations">
The Recipient shall: (a) keep the Discloser's Confidential Information confidential; (b) use it only for the Purpose; and (c) not disclose it to any person except its employees, officers, professional advisers and subcontractors who need to know it for the Purpose and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement.
</approved_clause>
<approved_clause id="nda-definition" title="Definition of Confidential Information">
"Confidential Information" means all information of a confidential nature disclosed by or on behalf of one party (the "Discloser") to the other party (the "Recipient"), whether before or after the date of this Agreement, in any form, including business, technical, financial and product information, and any information that is marked as confidential or would reasonably be regarded as confidential.
</approved_clause>
<approved_clause id="nda-exclusions" title="Exclusions from Confidential Information">
Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this Agreement; (b) was lawfully in the Recipient's possession before disclosure; (c) is lawfully received from a third party without restriction; or (d) is independently developed by the Recipient without use of the Discloser's Confidential Information.
</approved_clause>

Our standard positions:
<standard_position id="pb-governing-law" title="Governing law and jurisdiction">
Our standard: Law of England and Wales, with the courts of England and Wales having exclusive jurisdiction.
Acceptable fallback: Law of Ireland or Scotland; or English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction. Any US state law needs General Counsel sign-off.
Red flags: Any US state law; Exclusive jurisdiction of courts outside the UK; Arbitration seated outside London
</standard_position>
<standard_position id="pb-confidentiality-term" title="Duration of confidentiality obligations">
Our standard: Obligations survive for 3 years after termination or expiry; trade secrets protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.
Acceptable fallback: Anywhere from 2 to 5 years after termination.
Red flags: Perpetual obligations for all information; Less than 2 years; No survival clause
</standard_position>
<standard_position id="pb-mutuality" title="Mutuality">
Our standard: Every confidentiality obligation, restriction and remedy applies equally to both parties.
Acceptable fallback: None. A one-way NDA must be on our one-way template.
Red flags: Obligations that bind only PortSwigger; Remedies or indemnities available to one party only
</standard_position>
<standard_position id="pb-residuals" title="Residuals">
Our standard: No residuals clause. The Recipient may not use Confidential Information retained in memory outside the Purpose.
Acceptable fallback: None. We have never accepted a residuals clause; escalate to General Counsel.
Red flags: Right to use information retained in unaided memory; Any "notwithstanding" language that frees use of Confidential Information
</standard_position>
<standard_position id="pb-non-solicit" title="Non-solicitation of staff">
Our standard: No non-solicitation clause.
Acceptable fallback: Mutual, no more than 12 months, limited to staff directly involved, with a carve-out for general job advertisements.
